Answer: B
Reason: The imaging sequence demonstrates initial bilateral opacities (Figure 1) progressing to severe, dense consolidations (Figure 4), followed by complete radiological resolution (Figures 5a/5b). This rapid progression and subsequent clearance within a short timeframe is characteristic of alveolar hemorrhage associated with Weil Syndrome (severe leptospirosis), distinguishing it from conditions like Goodpasture syndrome or typical bacterial pneumonia which have different temporal courses or residual findings.
